scope: independent read-only source review, not browser or hosted-site testing
reviewed: Denominator uses the complete validated source level before access filtering; union by phrase identity removes repeated presentations. Templates, received turns and preparations outside phraseIds are excluded.
Known persistence uses explicit currentPhrase.id and pair ID; no credit is inferred from advancing, listening, completing themes, previous review absence or classic storage.

Storage entries are restricted to known pairs and bounded strings; intersection with the source identity set bounds the numerator; integer percentage floors the exact ratio, so 100 requires all cards.
A revoir removes explicit known status; ordinary removal from the reminder list does not add known status. Existing access and template/received guards stay in place.
V1 saveCardDecision delegates directly to the old review save, preserving its previous write/error behavior. V1 keeps the old level quantity label.

Only the modern theme overview sets progressbar semantics and the localized level label. All other screens clear level ARIA attributes and preserve their prior lesson/sequence counters and visual progress.
Source load generation guard precedes denominator assignment; delayed old levels cannot replace the active denominator.
Cross-tab known storage events reload the known map; writes reload current stored pairs before mutation.
limitations: Progress is local to this browser profile/device, not synchronized to an authenticated account or between devices.
Classic ox_known_<lang> uses study-text keys and is deliberately neither migrated nor changed. Previous modern Je connais decisions were not durable and cannot be recovered.

If the progress write fails after a reminder write, the previous reminder list is restored. The rollback is best-effort if storage also refuses that rollback; the action returns failure and does not advance or claim successful persistence.
The existing desktop Continuer behavior is unchanged; Je connais still follows the existing explicit right-swipe action rather than implying acquisition from lesson completion.
